Write a natural short email exchange. Subject: Dinner. Participants: Me, Ben; Me is the owner's speaker label, not a spoken name. Date: 2026-10-13, local time 10:00–13:45.
Earlier messages in this same thread, with their dates (context, not text to repeat):
2026-10-12 Ben: Hi! Following up on the dinner we arranged in DM to pass along the address.

It's Juniper Cafe, 48 Maple Ave. Are we still good for 7pm next Thursday, Oct 22?
2026-10-12 Me: Hi Ben! Yes, that's the same one from our DMs.

Confirming Thursday, Oct 22 at 7pm at Juniper Cafe. Thanks for sending the address — see you there!
2026-10-12 Ben: Perfect, confirmed — 7pm Thursday at Juniper Cafe. See you then!
Continue naturally. People remember the prior exchange and do not recap settled details unless conversation calls for it. Respect any gap between those dates and today's date; don't reply as if an old message just arrived.

Scenario: Ben replies to their existing email thread from work to reschedule dinner from Thursday October 22 to Saturday October 24. Include a faithful quoted copy of the actual earlier Thursday email underneath his new reply, preserving its wording and address. The user accepts the change.

The conversation must naturally and unambiguously establish each of these facts (they are authoring constraints, not lines to copy):
1. Ben asks to move dinner from Thursday October 22 to Saturday October 24 because of a work deadline. The user agrees to 7 pm at Juniper Cafe on October 24.
2. The old Thursday-at-7 details appear in quoted email history after the reschedule, faithfully copying the actual earlier email including Juniper Cafe's address.
Use 2–6 short emails. The subject is header metadata; do not put a Subject: prefix inside an email body. Copy quoted earlier messages faithfully; never invent different addresses, dates or wording for them. Return only JSON with dialogue (an array of {"sender": "Name", "body": "email text"}) and writer_note (a short string). Bodies may contain paragraphs and quoted replies using escaped newlines.
